newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs criticise Cossack units on Russian border.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs criticise Cossack units on Russian border.

text.p: In a further sign that a customs union between Russia and three ex-Soviet states is crumbling, Kazakhstan on Tuesday criticised what it said were armed Cossack units placed along the republic's northern border with Russia.

"In some Russian regions along the Kazakh border, the Russian Federation has set up Cossack posts," Beksultan Sarsekov, secretary of Kazakhstan's Security Council, told a news conference in the capital Almaty.
The Cossacks, a warrior class of ethnic Slavs which rolled back Russia's vast frontiers in Tsarist times, reappeared in diminished form during the Soviet collapse.

"These Cossacks received uniforms and weapons (from Russia)," said Sarsekov, saying this was at odds with an open borders agreement with Russia. "These Cossacks are a prototype border guard force," he said.

Last week, a senior Kazakh customs official said the former Soviet republic planned to turn its back on the customs union with Belarus and neighbours Russia and Kyrgyzstan, saying the union was damaging to the Kazakh economy.
Russian foreign ministry officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.
Kazakhstan has said it aims to join the World Trade Organisation and has pledged open trade policies.

Sarsekov said the customs union would figure on the agenda at Friday's Commonwealth of Independent States summit in Moscow, adding that it pointed to a general failure of integration between the 12-member grouping of ex-Soviet republics.
"Kazakhstan is for CIS integration. We have long hoped and still hope that Russia be the nucleus of this integration. But this has not happened," Sarsekov said.
Kazakhstan, with a large population of ethnic Russians and reliant on Russian pipelines for oil exports, is normally extremely cautious in its relations with the Kremlin.
